answer: Give every identity a purse of work credits earned only by finishing checkable jobs for strangers, and charge credits for each new right it claims. A quill of earned credit cannot be bought or transferred, so a farm must do real work for every fake it mints. Like a river that only flows downhill, credits drain when spent and refill only through fresh, verified labour; idle copies starve. Each spend is published, and strangers may audit any claim, so a zephyr of empty identities cannot inflate itself into influence, because every right is paid for in honest work, one job at a time.
